ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A ride at an amusement park consists of a hollow cylinder with a student placed against the wall as shown. When the cylinder rotates quickly enough, the student is able to lift her feet off the floor and remain stuck to the wall. In terms of the student's mass \( m \), the radius of the cylinder \( r \), the coefficient of static friction \( \mu \) between the student and the wall, and fundamental quantities, determine the minimum rotational velocity \( \omega \) that the ride can have while still allowing the student to stick to the wall and not slide down.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a vertically placed hollow cylindrical amusement ride, and the cylinder rotates around the vertical axis in the middle. In the figure, the arrow pointing from the central axis to the cylinder wall is labeled r, indicating the radius; at the bottom there is a red curved arrow labeled omega, indicating the angular velocity; at the inner wall on the right, a red student is drawn, with m labeled beside it, indicating the student's mass. The student leans against the inner wall of the cylinder, with the feet leaving the ground. Reasoning: After the student's feet leave the ground, the support in the vertical direction can only come from the static friction force exerted by the wall on the student. Force analysis on the student: gravity mg is downward; static friction force f_s is upward, preventing the student from sliding down; the normal force N exerted by the wall on the student points horizontally toward the center of the cylinder. The student undergoes circular motion with radius r and angular velocity omega together with the cylinder, so the normal force provides the centripetal force: N = m omega^2 r. When the student is just not sliding down, the static friction force reaches its maximum value and balances gravity: f_s,max = mu N = mg. Substituting N gives mu m omega^2 r = mg. Canceling m, we get omega^2 = g/(mu r), therefore the minimum angular velocity is omega_min = sqrt(g/(mu r)).

raw_record.question_text: A ride at an amusement park consists of a hollow cylinder with a student placed against the wall as shown. When the cylinder rotates quickly enough, the student is able to lift her feet off the floor and remain stuck to the wall. In terms of the student's mass \(m\), the radius of the cylinder \(r\), the coefficient of static friction \(\mu\) between the student and the wall, and fundamental quantities, determine the minimum rotational velocity \(\omega\) that the ride can have while still allowing the student to stick to the wall and not slide down.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a vertical hollow cylinder rotating about a central vertical axis, with radius labeled r from the axis to the wall, angular speed labeled omega, and the student of mass m pressed against the inner wall. From the text, use that the student's feet are off the floor, so the only vertical support is static friction with the wall. In the inertial/lab frame, draw forces on the student: weight mg downward, static friction f_s upward, and wall normal force N horizontally inward toward the rotation axis. The normal force provides centripetal force, so N = m omega^2 r. At the minimum angular speed, friction is at its maximum and just balances weight: f_s,max = mu N = mg. Substitute N to get mu m omega^2 r = mg, cancel m, and solve omega_min = sqrt(g/(mu r)).

图像描述：图中显示一个竖直放置的空心圆柱形 amusement ride，圆柱绕中间的竖直轴旋转。图上从中心轴指向圆柱壁的箭头标为 r，表示半径；底部有红色弯曲箭头标为 omega，表示角速度；右侧内壁处画有一个红色学生，旁边标有 m，表示学生质量。学生靠在圆柱内壁上，脚离开地面。

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the student is shown stuck to the inside wall of a rotating vertical cylinder, with the rotation axis through the center, radius r to the wall, and angular speed omega. claims.claim: The normal force provides the centripetal force.

claims.claim: In this problem, the normal force satisfies N = m omega^2 r.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: N = m omega^2 r

claims.claim: When just not sliding down, the static friction force reaches its maximum value.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: When it is necessary to just not slide down, the static friction force reaches its maximum value

claims.claim: When just not sliding down, the static friction force balances gravity.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: and balances gravity

claims.claim: In this problem, the maximum static friction satisfies f_s,max = mu N.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: In this problem, when it is just not sliding down, mu N = mg.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: Substituting N gives mu m omega^2 r = mg.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: Canceling m, obtain omega^2 = g/(mu r).

claims.claim: The minimum angular speed is omega_min = sqrt(g/(mu r)).
